doc.title: Eddie Metz Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 3, 2015

title: Playing club dates and jazz standards as a teenager in Ann Arbor
summary: From age 14 he played dance gigs of standards, bossa novas and Dixieland at a pizza place; a pause to turn off the heater.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah, but see when I was growing up, in the 60s and 70s, and probably you too, I had all this jazz coming at me and I was playing gigs starting at age 14, playing dance gigs on the weekend. And it was mostly jazz. We played three rock songs.
Define what kind of jazz it was.
Oh it’d be standards. “Take the A Train.”
I’m going to pause for a second and turn off the heater.
You can splice this I’m sure.
I did the same thing yesterday.
Yeah so that was what kind of jazz?

Well it was what we call club dates. Standards for dancing at a country club in Ann Arbor, Michigan. So we played bossa novas, we played rumbas, we played cha-chas, we played straight ahead jazz songs, Duke Ellington ballads. Nothing too fast, nothing too slow. It was businessman’s bounce. You know, and ballads were like [scats and snaps fingers]. That was about as slow as it got. And then the faster tune [scats and snaps fingers]. It was for dancing. Nothing too fast. Nothing too slow. So that’s where I really cut my teeth. I also was playing Dixieland gigs at a local pizza place. So I was getting that. But then on the radio I listened to all this rock & roll.
